title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Jordan Lee
content:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical company handbook content relevant to: what it's like to work here, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and the internal tools new hires need to be productive. It is intended for new employees, hiring managers, people-ops partners, and leads who run interviews and onboarding.

1) Working at Redwood — our culture and expectations

Introduction
- Redwood is a small-to-midsize, engineering-first company focused on production LLM inference. We prioritize shipping reliable, low-latency services and giving engineers end-to-end ownership.
- Core values: Customer-first reliability, engineering craftsmanship, pragmatic experimentation, open documentation, and inclusive collaboration.

Day-to-day expectations
- Deliver incremental improvements with clear ownership (tickets should include acceptance criteria).
- Communicate asynchronously first (Confluence + Slack), escalate on-call issues via PagerDuty.
- Participate in a weekly team retrospective and a monthly all-hands.

Performance & reviews
- Review cadence: quarterly check-ins + annual performance review.
- Goals: OKR-aligned goals set quarterly by teams. Expect 2–4 measurable objectives per review period.
- Promotion cycle: formal calibration happens semi-annually; managers nominate candidates using the career ladder rubric.

2) Roles & career ladders (summary)

Scope and approach
- Redwood maintains role definitions across Engineering, Product, SRE, Applied ML, Design, and GTM functions. The ladder separates IC (individual contributor) and people manager tracks. Titles reflect scope and impact rather than compensation bands alone.

Engineering ladder (condensed)
- IC1 / Associate Engineer: Contributes to small features, asks for guidance, writes tests and docs.
- IC2 / Software Engineer: Owns medium features, writes design docs, performs code reviews, mentors interns.
- IC3 / Senior Engineer: Leads major components, owns services and SLOs, influences design across squads.
- IC4 / Staff Engineer: Cross-team technical leadership, architecture ownership, and mentoring senior peers.
- IC5 / Principal Engineer: Company-level technical strategy, drive for scalability and long-term architecture.

Manager track
- Mgr1 / Engineering Manager: Manages a small team (4–8), responsible for delivery and people growth.
- Mgr2 / Senior Eng Manager: Multiple teams or a large product area, owns delivery and hiring plans.
- Dir/VP: Strategic leadership, org design, cross-functional alignment.

Promotion guidance (high level)
1. Demonstrated impact beyond current scope.
2. Clear examples of mentorship and ownership.
3. Strong feedback from peers and cross-functional partners.
4. Alignment with ladder competencies (technical, execution, communication).

Documentation & artifacts required for promotion submission
- Updated resume-style summary (1 page).
- 3–5 concrete impact examples with metrics.
- Manager assessment and 3 peer reviews.
- Draft promotion statement (manager-written).

3) Benefits, compensation, and perks (overview)

Compensation philosophy
- Market-competitive base + equity + benefits. Compensation reviewed annually; adjustments follow performance review cycles and market benchmarking.

Health & wellness
- Medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options. Redwood pays a majority of employee-only premiums.
- Flexible health spending options (HSA/FSA).

Time off and parental leave
- PTO: Flexible paid time off with a recommended minimum of 15 days per year for new hires; managers approve based on coverage.
- Parental leave: Primary parent up to 18 weeks paid; secondary parent up to 8 weeks. Additional return-to-work support available.

Financial & retirement
- 401(k) with company match starting after 90 days.
- Annual stipend for home office equipment and professional development.

Perks & workplace support
- Remote-first with company hubs in NA and EU. Travel allowance for annual in-person offsite.
- Monthly wellness stipend, learning budget ($1,500/year), and conference allowance.
- Commuter benefits and mental health resources (EAP).

Security and compliance benefits for Private customers
- Employees who work directly on Private deployments have mandatory training and an additional compliance stipend; see security-and-compliance runbook for details.

4) Hiring overview — process and expectations

Inclusive hiring principles
- Structured interviews and rubrics required for all roles. Candidate scorecards must capture competency alignment and cultural add.
- Diverse interview panels: aim for at least one interviewer from outside the hiring team.

Standard interview flow (software engineering example)
1. Recruiter screen (30–45 minutes): role fit, compensation expectations, timeline.
2. Hiring manager screen (45 minutes): team fit, high-level technical discussions.
3. Technical assessment (take-home or coding exercise) OR live code pair (60 minutes) based on role level.
4. Onsite loop (4–6 interviews, 2–3 hours virtual or in-person): system design, debugging/problem solving, culture/values conversation, and collaborator interviews.
5. Debrief & calibration: interviewers submit scorecards within 48 hours; hiring manager synthesizes feedback.
6. Offer & negotiation: People Ops owns offer paperwork and reference checks.

Time-to-hire targets
- Target time from first recruiter screen to offer: 21 calendar days for most roles.

Hiring manager checklist (pre-offer)
- Role brief and rubric created and approved.
- Interview panel confirmed and trained on unconscious bias.
- Scorecards and evaluation criteria documented in the job posting.
- Compensation band and hiring timeline approved by People Ops.

5) New hire onboarding and 0–90 day plan

Pre-start checklist (People Ops + hiring manager)
- Offer accepted and paperwork completed.
- Accounts provisioned: Okta, Google Workspace, GitHub, Jira, Confluence, Slack, cloud console read-only.
- Hardware ordered and shipped (if applicable) with tracking.
- First-week schedule and buddy assigned.

Day 0–7: Orientation and foundation
- Company orientation (People Ops): benefits overview, payroll setup, code of conduct, security training.
- Team onboarding: meet-and-greets, review team roadmap, setup dev environment.
- Deliverable: Clone repo, run integration tests locally, and submit a short "first week" retrospective.

Day 8–30: Contribution ramp
- Assigned 1–2 small tickets for production or docs changes.
- Scheduled 1:1s weekly with manager and buddy check-ins.
- Deliverable: Production change or documentation PR merged; short tech review presentation to team.

Day 31–90: Ownership and performance objectives
- Take ownership of a small service or feature area.
- Set 90-day goals aligned to team OKRs.
- Participation in on-call rotation where applicable (shadow first).
- Deliverable: A post-90 day summary of impact and a roadmap for the next quarter.

6) Internal tools guide (onboarding essentials)

Access & identity
- Okta: Single Sign-On for all company apps. Mandatory MFA via Authenticator or hardware token.
- Google Workspace: Email, Calendar, Drive. Shared team drives are provisioned by request.

Communication & docs
- Slack: Primary synchronous communication. Channels are prefixed by team (e.g., #eng-serving-runtime) and by topic (#infra-updates). Use status and Do-Not-Disturb when heads-down.
- Confluence: Our source-of-truth for runbooks, architectures, and handbook. Add or update docs when you make process changes.

Engineering & product tools
- GitHub: Main code hosting. Protect main branches and follow the branching policy (branch-per-feature + PR review + CI checks).
- Jira: Issue tracking and sprint planning. Tickets should include clear acceptance criteria and estimation.
- CI/CD (Buildkite): Pipelines trigger on PRs and merges; non-blocking checks allowed for experimental branches.

Observability & incident tooling
- Datadog: Metrics and dashboards for services. Dashboards are owned by service owners.
- Sentry: Error aggregation for user-facing services.
- PagerDuty: On-call routing and escalation. Follow the on-call runbook for paging thresholds.

Security & secrets
- Vault / KMS: Secrets storage; do not store credentials in source or documents.
- Security training: Complete the mandatory secure sdlc and compliance training within first 14 days.

How to request access
1. Submit an access request via the internal IT portal (linked in Confluence).
2. Manager approval is required for elevated cloud permissions.
3. Access is provisioned within 48 business hours for standard requests.

7) Ownership and escalation

Document ownership
- People Ops maintains handbook content. Teams are responsible for keeping team-specific runbooks and role descriptions up to date.
- Owner metadata: add an "owner" line at the top of any Confluence page you maintain.

Escalation process
- For people issues: contact People Ops or your People Business Partner.
- For security incidents: follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security runbook and page Security immediately.
- For production incidents: follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process and notify SRE leads.

Appendices

A. Quick links (add to your onboarding checklist)
- Confluence handbook home: /confluence/company-handbook
- Access request portal: /internal/it/access-requests
- GitHub org: https://github.com/redwood-inference
- Slack workspace: internal invite link provided during onboarding

B. Sample 90-day goal template (to paste into your 1:1)
- Goal 1 (Impact): Reduce 95th percentile latency of service X by 15% by end of quarter.
- Goal 2 (Quality): Decrease retry rate for inference pipeline Y by 20% (monitor via Datadog).
- Goal 3 (Growth): Mentor an intern and run a tech talk.

C. Contacts and owners
- People Ops lead: Jordan Lee (people-ops).
- Head of Eng (product-facing infra): Marcus Chen.
- Security contact: Priya Nair.

If you have changes or suggested improvements to this handbook page, please open an edit and add your name to the page history, or file a PR with People Ops for significant policy updates.

End of document.
